analysis: 글로벌 금리·인플레이션: 2026년 4월 16일 기준 글로벌 통화정책 환경은 스태그플레이션적 구속 상태가 지속되고 있다. 미 연준은 IMF가 공식 산정한 관세 발 PCE +0.5% 인플레이션으로 인해 금리인하가 봉쇄된 상태이며, 성장 둔화 압력에도 불구하고 동결 기조를 유지하고 있다. 한국은행은 2.50%에서 동결을 유지하면서 AI 구조적 디플레이션을 G20 중앙은행 최초로 공식 통화정책 변수로 인정했다. BOK의 AI 디플레이션 인정은 향후 데이터에 따라 인플레이션 제약 없이 금리인하 여력이 있음을 시사한다. 그러나 호르무즈 봉쇄로 인한 에너지 수입 비용 인플레이션이 BOK의 인하 타이밍을 압박하고 있다. 한국 수출입·환율: 원달러 환율이 1,500원 임박 위협을 받는 상황에서 국민연금이 해외투자 환헤지 비율을 10%에서 15%로 긴급 확대한 것은 주권급 리스크 관리자 차원에서 현재 원화 약세가 구조적 요인에 의한 것임을 공식 확인한 신호다. 원화 약세의 복합 요인은 (1) 연준 동결로 인한 달러 강세, (2) 호르무즈 봉쇄로 인한 에너지 수입 비용 증가로 인한 무역수지 압박, (3) 중동전쟁·이란 제재 이슈에서 비롯된 한국 자산 지정학적 프리미엄 확대다. 방산·조선 수출은 역대 최고 수준(섹터 스코어 각각 239·238.5)이며, HBM 수출 YoY +180% 성장이 구조적 지지를 제공하고 있다. 이재명 정부는 중동전을 계기로 호르무즈 의존도 축소를 위한 대체 공급망 개척, 산업구조 개편, 탈플라스틱 전환을 국가 핵심 3대 프로젝트로 지정해 중기적으로 방산·에너지전환 섹터 수혜가 예상된다. 미중 무역갈등·관세 리스크: 미국 AI 안보법(중국 AI 칩 수입 전면 금지, Huawei Ascend 910C 명시)은 글로벌 AI 공급망을 재편하는 기술 탈동조화 변곡점이다. 중국은 이란 무기 공급 의혹을 추가 관세의 구실로 사용할 경우 '단호히 대응'할 것을 경고했으며, 이는 이란 분쟁과 미중 무역 갈등이 서로 강화하는 피드백 루프를 형성해 한국 수출기업에 대한 복합 리스크를 높이고 있다. 한국계 미셸 박 스틸의 주한 미국대사 지명(대중 강경파, 하원 중국특위 활동)은 한미 AI·반도체 MOU 이행 강화 및 중국 기술 공급망 탈동조화 압력 증가 신호다. 사이버보안 섹터 스코어 333(전 섹터 최고)은 AI 안보법에 의한 기업 AI 보안 지출 가속을 반영한다.
key_points: 원달러 1,500원 임박 — 국민연금 환헤지 15%로 긴급 확대, 원화 구조적 약세 공식 확인
호르무즈 봉쇄 지속 — 한국 원유 수입 70% 경유, 에너지 수입 인플레이션이 BOK 금리인하 여력 압박
미 연준 동결 확정 — IMF 산정 관세발 PCE +0.5% 인플레이션으로 금리인하 조기 불가
중국 '단호한 대응' 경고 — 이란 무기 공급 의혹 빌미로 추가 관세 시 보복 예고, 한국 수출 이중 노출
미셸 박 스틸 대중 강경파 주한 미국대사 지명 — 한미 AI·반도체 MOU 이행 강화, 대중 디커플링 압력 증가
이재명 3대 프로젝트(대체 공급망·산업구조 개편·탈플라스틱) — 방산·에너지전환·첨단제조 중기 수혜
BOK AI 디플레이션 공식 인정 — G20 첫 사례, 데이터 확인 시 하반기 1-2회 인하 여력 내포
사이버보안 섹터 스코어 333 (전체 최고) — AI 안보법+AI 거버넌스로 엔터프라이즈 보안 지출 구조적 가속
방산 239·조선 238.5 — NATO 결속 리스크·유럽 재무장·미 쇄빙선 협력이 구조적 수요 뒷받침
중국 유조선 호르무즈 봉쇄 돌파 성공 — 미국 제재 실효성 의문, 달러 기축통화 프리미엄 장기 침식 리스크

macro_environment.global_summary: The global macro environment as of April 16, 2026 is defined by three interlocking structural forces: (1) a deepening US-China technology and trade bifurcation that is accelerating de-globalization across supply chains; (2) a constrained monetary policy regime where AI-driven structural deflation is in tension with tariff-driven goods inflation, leaving major central banks in a prolonged hold; and (3) an escalating European rearmament cycle driven by erosion of US defense commitment to NATO. These three forces create a highly differentiated investment landscape — bearish for trade-exposed cyclicals dependent on globalized supply chains, but powerfully bullish for cybersecurity, defense, and shipbuilding sectors that are direct beneficiaries of the geopolitical restructuring. The EnvironmentScan TESE category distribution (P=238, T=94, E=85, S=47) confirms that geopolitical/regulatory dynamics are the dominant signal category this week, outnumbering technology signals 2.5x — an unusually high ratio that signals peak policy uncertainty. The multiple US Department of Commerce antidumping/countervailing duty actions against China (steel fluid end blocks, aluminum extrusions, oil country tubular goods, citric acid, frozen fish) visible in the April 14-16 P-category signals confirm that the US trade enforcement apparatus is running at peak operational tempo, with China as the primary target. This is not cyclical trade friction but structural economic decoupling in execution.
macro_environment.us_outlook: The US macro outlook is characterized by stagflationary undertow — tariff-driven inflation preventing accommodative monetary policy while growth faces headwinds from supply chain disruption and policy uncertainty. The IMF's April 2026 Article IV US Consultation formally quantified the tariff shock at +0.5% PCE inflation and -0.5% output impact, confirming the dual-constraint nature of the current policy bind. The Federal Reserve remains on hold: cutting rates into tariff-driven inflation would be a policy error, but the output drag prevents outright tightening. The April 16 P-signal confirming antidumping actions against China across steel, aluminum, oil tubulars, and citric acid signals that the trade enforcement escalation is accelerating rather than plateauing. The Presidential Declaration of a Major Disaster for Mississippi signals that fiscal spending on domestic infrastructure/disaster relief will partially offset the tariff drag. Net assessment: US economy is growing below potential (est. 1.5-2.0% annualized in Q2 2026), with inflation stubbornly above 3%, creating a Fed held captive by its own constraints. This is a 'muddle-through' scenario for the US economy — not recession but not strong enough to drive broad risk appetite.
macro_environment.korea_outlook: Korea's macro environment shows acute bifurcation: export volumes to China under pressure from the technology decoupling and antidumping dynamics, while defense and AI-linked exports are surging. The Korean won remains under structural depreciation pressure from USD strength and tariff uncertainty, though the Samsung HBM4 supply contract win and the Korea-US AI/Semiconductor MOU provide partial offsets via foreign inflow dynamics. The Bank of Korea held rates at 2.50% in April 2026, explicitly incorporating AI-driven structural deflation as a new monetary policy variable — this is the most analytically important Korean monetary policy development in years. The implication is that BOK will not reflexively cut on deflationary signals if those signals originate from AI productivity gains rather than demand weakness. KOSPI is benefiting from selective foreign buying in the AI/semiconductor and defense sectors, but broad market upside is constrained by global macro headwinds and high valuation in defense names. Today's stock data confirms the bifurcation: cybersecurity names (AhnLab +6.96%, Fasoo +29.85%, Igloo Security +11.23%) and shipbuilding (HD Hyundai Heavy +4.11%, Hanwha Ocean +2.62%) are outperforming sharply, while defense names show more muted moves (Hanwha Aerospace +1.26%, LIG Nex1 -0.62%). The Fasoo +29.85% move is a particularly strong signal — it implies a specific catalyst (possible cybersecurity contract announcement or new customer), and the 2,227.98% operating income growth validates the momentum.
macro_environment.fed_stance: The Federal Reserve is in a firmly data-dependent hold. The most recent FOMC communication signals that the dual mandate is experiencing genuine tension: tariff-driven inflation (PCE +0.5% from tariffs per IMF) is fighting against AI-driven structural deflation (BOK's acknowledgment of this phenomenon is a leading indicator for Fed thinking). The base case is zero rate changes through Q3 2026, with the first potential cut only materializing if: (a) tariff inflation proves transitory and PCE reverts below 2.5%, or (b) US labor market deteriorates sharply. Neither condition appears imminent. The risk scenario is that tariff escalation into China forces the Fed to consider a rate increase if inflation expectations de-anchor — a low probability (est. 10%) but non-trivial tail risk. For Korean markets, the Fed hold means the KRW/USD rate will remain at elevated levels (est. 1,380-1,420 range), which is a mixed signal: it pressures import costs and external debt service, but supports the competitiveness of Korean exporters priced in KRW. Net: Fed stance is modestly negative for Korean domestic demand but neutral-to-positive for Korean export sector.

4week_forecast.base_case: Over the 4-week period from 2026-04-16 to 2026-05-14, the dominant macro regime remains 'selective bifurcation': US-China trade decoupling accelerates in the background while AI infrastructure investment provides a countervailing growth engine. The Fed holds at current levels. BOK holds at 2.50%. KRW oscillates in the 1,380-1,420/USD range, with mild depreciation bias. The KOSPI trades in the 2,800-3,000 range, with outperformance concentrated in cybersecurity (sector score 332), shipbuilding (238), and defense (238) relative to the broader index. The primary catalysts to watch in the next 4 weeks are: (1) any US-China bilateral trade negotiation progress — even a temporary tariff pause would be a significant risk-on catalyst for global equities; (2) Q1 2026 earnings season confirming cybersecurity and shipbuilding revenue acceleration; (3) NATO defense ministers' meeting expected in late April — any US commitment softening or hardening will directly impact Korean defense export narrative. Base case probability: 55%. Base case confidence level: medium-high.
4week_forecast.bull_case: The bull case (probability ~25%) involves a combination of: (1) US-China technical working group makes unexpected progress on a limited tariff rollback in selected non-strategic sectors, triggering a broad risk-on rally that lifts the KOSPI above 3,000; (2) Q1 Korean corporate earnings surprise to the upside in shipbuilding and cybersecurity — both sectors showed strong momentum in today's price action, and a revenue beat would accelerate foreign inflow; (3) The Fasoo +29.85% move today proves to be the beginning of a re-rating of the Korean cybersecurity small-cap universe as institutional investors rotate into underfollowed names ahead of a major government cybersecurity framework announcement. In the bull case, KOSPI reaches 3,100-3,200 by mid-May and Korean defense names complete a final valuation expansion driven by confirmation of new European export contracts. KRW strengthens to 1,340-1,360/USD on foreign net inflows. The bull case is primarily driven by policy surprise, not fundamental change.
4week_forecast.bear_case: The bear case (probability ~20%) involves one or more of: (1) US tariff escalation expands to electronics or semiconductor components — either as retaliation for Chinese rare earth export controls or as new sector-specific actions; this would directly threaten the Korea-US semiconductor supply chain and cause sharp foreign selling of Korean tech; (2) Chinese retaliatory measures against Korea escalate beyond current levels — e.g., informal pressure on Korean brands in China, export license restrictions on rare earth materials critical to Korean defense manufacturing; (3) El Nino development (62% probability per Yale Climate Connections) hits agriculture and Pacific logistics hard, driving commodity inflation that forces the Fed to consider rate increases, causing global risk-off and EM capital outflows that hit KRW hard (1,450+ target). In the bear case, KOSPI tests 2,600-2,700 support, and even the high-conviction cybersecurity and defense names would see 10-15% drawdowns as multiple compression offsets earnings strength. The bear case is a 'simultaneous shocks' scenario, not a single-factor outcome.

sector_macro_impact.cybersecurity: STRONGEST MACRO TAILWIND. Multiple converging macro forces drive outperformance: (1) US AI National Security Act's Chinese AI chip total import ban creates a compliance-driven wave of enterprise AI security reviews across Korean corporations, financial institutions, and government agencies; (2) The 7 US Arms Sales Notifications in the April 14 P-signals confirm an active allied defense procurement cycle — allied nations building up military capabilities also require integrated cybersecurity architecture; (3) AI governance pressure across TESE signals consistently flags cybersecurity compliance as a required corporate spending item. Today's price action validates the thesis: AhnLab +6.96% (PER 14.19x, still reasonable), Fasoo +29.85% (potential catalyst event), Igloo Security +11.23% (turnaround continuation). The sector score of 332 — the highest in the universe — is supported by genuine fundamental momentum. Macro recommendation: overweight, with AhnLab as core and Igloo as tactical.
sector_macro_impact.defense: STRONG MACRO TAILWIND WITH VALUATION CAUTION. The NATO cohesion risk (15% US withdrawal probability from prior analysis), European rearmament acceleration, and Middle East AI-military spend are all structurally constructive. The 7 Arms Sales Notifications in the April 14 signals confirm that US FMS approvals are running at high volume — these create reference prices and capability benchmarks that Korean defense exporters can compete against. However, valuation has become a headwind: Hanwha Aerospace at PER 53.48x, Hyundai Rotem at 30.55x, Hanwha Systems at 102.73x, and LIG Nex1 at 77.07x represent premium multiples that require perfect execution and continued earnings acceleration. Today's mixed performance (Hanwha Aero +1.26%, LIG Nex1 -0.62%) suggests the market is beginning to discriminate within the sector. Macro recommendation: selectively overweight, prefer Hyundai Rotem (PER 30.55x most reasonable in sector) and Hanwha Systems as a call option on electronics integration; avoid LIG Nex1 on valuation grounds.
sector_macro_impact.shipbuilding: SOLID MACRO TAILWIND, EXECUTION-DEPENDENT. Global LNG trade restructuring (Europe replacing Russian gas supply chains permanently), naval vessel demand from NATO members and allied Pacific nations, and the durable backlog effect are all constructive. Today's strong performance — HD Hyundai Heavy +4.11%, Hanwha Ocean +2.62%, Samsung Heavy +0.71% — confirms market confidence. However, the antidumping actions against China in steel and aluminum (April 14-16 P-signals) create materials cost uncertainty for Korean shipbuilders who source some inputs globally. HD Korea Shipbuilding (009540) at PER 13.28x remains the most attractively valued name with market cap 28.8 trillion won. HD Hyundai Heavy Industries (329180) at 51.9 trillion market cap and PER 31.46x is pricing in significant execution success on its LNG carrier backlog. Macro recommendation: overweight HD Korea Shipbuilding on valuation; neutral Hanwha Ocean given premium multiple (PER 31.75x, PBR 6.41x).
sector_macro_impact.ai_platform: POSITIVE MACRO TREND, LIMITED DIRECT KOREA EXPOSURE. The AI platform sector score of 134 reflects the global AI infrastructure build-out driven by Middle East sovereign wealth fund investment, US hyperscaler CapEx, and the Samsung HBM4/NVIDIA GB300 supply contract. However, the Korean watchlist does not include direct AI platform names — the AI platform exposure is captured indirectly through cybersecurity (AI security compliance), technology (semiconductor adjacency), and shipbuilding (data center power infrastructure). For the macro backdrop: the 'world's most concentrated AI infrastructure build-out' in the Middle East represents a durable demand anchor for AI-adjacent Korean exports. The India zero-tax AI workload incentive (February T-signal) signals that South Asian AI demand is materializing as a second wave. Macro implication: structurally supportive for any Korean technology company with AI infrastructure exposure.
sector_macro_impact.technology: STRUCTURALLY BULLISH, NEAR-TERM VOLATILITY. Technology sector score of 134 is driven by AI platform demand and semiconductor cycle strength. The Samsung HBM4 supply contract with NVIDIA, HBM exports +180% YoY, and the Korea-US AI/Semiconductor MOU are the foundational macro drivers. However, the technology sector faces the most direct exposure to US-China decoupling risk — any US export control expansion to semiconductor equipment or advanced materials would create significant disruption to Korean tech supply chains. The T-category signals (94 total) show continued acceleration in AI model development, AI agents, and multimodal AI capabilities, all of which require increasing memory bandwidth and therefore HBM demand. The AI deflation phenomenon acknowledged by BOK means tech-driven productivity gains are real and measurable at the macroeconomic level, validating the structural AI demand narrative. Macro recommendation: technology is the highest-conviction structural theme, but implementation must be selective given geopolitical exposure.
sector_macro_impact.consumer: NEUTRAL TO MODEST POSITIVE. Consumer sector score of 132 suggests moderate macro support — not a primary theme but not a headwind. The BOK hold at 2.50% is mildly supportive of domestic consumer spending by preventing further mortgage rate increases. Korean household debt remains high, capping the consumer recovery potential, but AI productivity gains are beginning to feed through to real wage growth in services sectors. The key macro risk for consumer is imported inflation from KRW weakness and tariff-driven global goods price increases. The Mississippi disaster declaration and US fiscal spending acceleration will stimulate US consumer demand, which creates indirect positive spillover for Korean consumer electronics exports. However, with the KRW under pressure and Chinese consumer competition intensifying in Korea's key export markets, consumer remains a lower-conviction theme relative to the structural macro tailwinds in cybersecurity and defense.
